literal: Every day, having investigated, justice not-administering king's, every day the country will be ruined.
translation: The country of a king who does not investigate and administer justice daily will ruin itself day by day.
modern: நாள்தோறும் ஆராய்ந்து நீதி வழங்காத அரசனுடைய நாடானது, நாள்தோறும் அழிவை நோக்கிச் செல்லும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the immediate and continuous consequences of negligent governance. The poet uses the word 'நாடொறும்' (every day) twice to establish a direct cause-and-effect relationship. If a ruler fails to investigate grievances ('நாடி') and deliver justice ('முறைசெய்யா') on a daily basis, the decline of the nation is not a distant event but a daily process of decay ('நாடு கெடும்'). Good governance requires constant vigilance, and its absence leads to the steady, day-by-day ruin of the state.
